scope: Final test-only sibling identity/order regression and 360px viewport hit-testing additions; not a curriculum-content or full regression verdict
checks: Independently verified patch and resulting file hashes; node --check succeeds.
Original state isolation, blank sibling, unchanged source record/progress and legacy mode assertions are retained or strengthened.

Two parameterized cases reorder only children array from route.fetch actual /api/session JSON. No child IDs, state, contents, authorization, HTTP status or API state response are fabricated. Real child-state fetches remain unmocked.

Both initial identities are asserted, then explicit source and sibling IDs are switched twice with loaded child status and exact observation/view-count assertions. Direct API reads independently confirm persisted source state and absence of copied sibling data.

360x640 case scrolls actual controls, checks viewport intersection and elementFromPoint center visibility, performs normal clicks/checks (no force), verifies active step and final ready preparation state. This tests interactive reachability, not just screenshot aesthetics.
Legacy/new record and sibling screenshots supplement assertions; viewport screenshots do not replace any assertion.
limitations: No browser execution or retry performed during this independent review. New assertions must execute successfully in hosted CI on exact integrated source.
Center hit-testing proves center clickability after scroll, not visibility of every control pixel or every device/layout.
Two session display orders test UI robustness; they intentionally do not assert or change server canonical ordering.
Initial failed-run actual child IDs remain unobserved; confirmed test ordering defect and deterministic SQL reproduction are described in prior report.
No edits to application or test source by reviewer, no remote writes, no production data access.
nextGate: Freeze the reviewed source after authorized integration, then require full exact-head regression CI; inspect emitted viewport screenshots before claiming visual acceptance.
